transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon. Pope Leo made his first public appearance
today since lung cancer surgery just days ago. Megan Williams reports from Rome.
An excited crowd greeted Pope Leo as he emerged from behind a curtain on his
balcony overlooking St. Peter's Square to give his Sunday Angelus blessing.
Speaking in a strong voice, the Pope thanked the faithful for their prayers
and his doctors at Rome's Jimmy Lee Hospital. He said his illness brought him closer to others
who suffer and promised to resume his duties gradually. Surgeons removed part of his right
lung Tuesday. His doctor says he could recover within 10 days and keep to travel plans to
South America next month. For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
Canadian Defence Minister David McGinty reports there are multiple casualties
after what he called a serious incident on a military base in Alberta.
I'm saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident
on the base. The Canadian Armed Forces, the Department of National Defence, partners across
the federal government, including public safety, are working with the government of Alberta and
the municipal governments to mobilize all necessary support and working through the details of what
actually occurred. McGinty describes the situation as "tragic." Fire crews in Southern California
are making headway as they battle the Norte Fire in San Juan Capistrano, saying the fire is about
25% contained. Steve Futterman reports. With the Santa and the winds slowly losing strength,
fire crews began making significant progress, establishing containment lines, going after hot
spots and preventing the fire from spreading. This allowed Orange County Sheriff's Captain Justin
Chevalier to make the announcement residents wanted to hear. We are pleased to announce the
lifting of the evacuation zones in San Juan Capistrano and San Clemente. Even though the worst
is clearly over, fire crews remain on the scene as they move towards putting the fire out completely.
They could get help the next few days as the forecast calls for rain on Tuesday and Wednesday.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in Los Angeles.
President Trump rallied on behalf of Republican candidates yesterday in Kentucky,
as he continues his multi-state swing in the remaining weeks before the midterms.
The president is vowed to make 35 stops, including in places where Republican candidates face tough
Democratic opposition, as well as in states that are solidly bred. Last week alone, the president
made stops in states including Alaska, Arizona, and Montana. This week, he has stops planned for
Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina, Iowa, and Florida. You're listening to NPR.
Deadlines for registering to vote for the midterm elections are coming up in several states.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has this rundown. Monday, October 19th, is the last chance for eligible
voters to register or update their registration in Alabama, Pennsylvania, and South Dakota.
The next major voter registration deadline is on Saturday, October 24th, in Massachusetts and New
York. And then October 31st, Halloween, is the last day in North Carolina for signing up in person
at the state's early voting sites. The only state where voter registration is not required is North
Dakota. And many states allow for same-day registration at the polls on November 3rd's
election day. If you're already registered in a state with an earlier deadline, election officials
recommend going to your state's official election website to confirm your status and contact
information before voter registration ends. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News. A report released by
congressional Democrats says President Trump's investments in pharmaceutical companies have
significantly increased since he began his second term. The report finds the president's
portfolio added millions of dollars in stocks from firms benefiting from a Republican-backed
law that shields certain medications from price negotiations under Medicare. Details show the
president's pharmaceutical stock holdings grew from $1.7 million in 2024 to as much as $56.2
million by the end of 2025. The White House denies any ethical issues and accuses the Democrats
of fabrication. I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Pope Leo makes first public appearance since lung cancer surgery, blessing crowd at St. Peter's Square
Canadian Defence Minister David McGinty reports multiple fatalities and injuries in serious incident at Alberta military base
Norte Fire in San Juan Capistrano about 25% contained; evacuation zones lifted in San Juan Capistrano and San Clemente
President Trump rallies for Republican candidates in Kentucky during multi-state midterm campaign swing
Voter registration deadlines approaching in Alabama, Pennsylvania, South Dakota, Massachusetts, New York, and North Carolina
Congressional Democrats report Trump's pharmaceutical stock holdings grew from $1.7 million to $56.2 million; White House denies wrongdoing
